summary.title: Part 5 - Improving the Frontend
summary.one_liner: You learn how to add a React chat input that sends messages on Enter to a Go WebSocket server, and how to render chat messages as styled components instead of raw JSON.
takeaways: Create a ChatInput React component that wraps an input and fires a handler on onKeyDown.
Check event.keyCode === 13 to detect Enter, send the input value over the WebSocket, then clear the field.
Create a Message component that parses a JSON string prop into state and renders its body.
Pass each chat history entry's data into Message components inside ChatHistory, replacing raw JSON display.
Style messages as boxed cards with box-shadow and border-radius using SCSS.
summary.summary: This is part 5 of a series building a chat application with a Go WebSocket backend and a ReactJS frontend. The post adds a ChatInput component whose onKeyDown handler sends the typed text on Enter and clears the field, then updates App.js to pass in the send function. It then creates a Message component that parses a JSON message prop and renders its body in a styled box, and wires it into the ChatHistory component.
